transcription: If you're a retro gaming fan, this place is your heaven. Located in none other than Otaku District, Akihabata, this is super potato. Don't ask me what the name has to do with anything, but this place has three floors of games and accessories that is quite literally a blast from the past. They have a particularly large collection of Nintendo games, most of which I never thought I'd see again. The top floor has some retro arcade games that you can actually play, so whether you're looking for that one specific game, or you just want to relive part of your childhood, definitely check it out.

caption:
this amazake or amasake shop is located behind a small shrine, it is a 9 minute walk from Fushimi Inari Tiasha, aka the Senbon Torii (thousand torii gates). 

don’t ask me how I found it, it was very randomly on google 360 but the point being, this place is run by the lovely lady, Suzuki Kazuyote. her warmth and hospitality is unparalleled as you can already see in the video. 

both hot and cold amazake are available here and it is just for ¥500 which is absolutely insane. 

for those wondering, what is amazake? amazake is a traditional sweet low or non-alcoholic japanese drink made with fermented rice. essentially the alcohol percentage separates it from sake. 

if you are visiting senbon torii then you need to cool off here after the long hike (this too is about a 500 meter hike) but everything is worth the break from the tourists and having a traditional experience. it truly surprises me how lowkey this place is and it is barely on anyone’s radar.

as much as i wanted to gatekeep it, I just couldn’t resist. 

📍あまざけ末富亭 (amazake suetomi-tei)
🍶〒612-0805 京都府京都市伏見区深草開土口町5-12

transcription: I flew all the way to Japan for a pair of sneakers and I bought the wrong ones. On itsuka tiger closed all their stores in the US and it's kind of hard to get them now but that's not why I waited until I visited Japan to pick them up. I did that because I'm crazy and willing to pay the gnarly price for the nippon maid series which are the sneakers made in Japan and to my knowledge only sold in Japan. Except I bought the wrong ones. I just got the regular mexico 66 SD's. I was seduced by the thinner laces. We were running late for a reservation and I didn't double check. I love the pairs I bought though, they are totally worth the hype. Nero shoes are super uncomfortable on my feet, but for some reason these are the only shoe that look narrow, but are also super comfy. They're like the perfect walking shoe. That said, I might go back and get the pair that I wanted, just in a different color.
